title: AI-enabled cyber risks to Singapore's financial system and critical infrastructure
asked: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked for the Government's assessment of risks from advanced AI models that could steal data or disrupt critical infrastructure, whether AI-enabled cyber risks are a new class of systemic financial risk, and what early-warning indicators or triggers are being developed; Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui also asked about frontier AI models such as Anthropic's Mythos and whether cybersecurity frameworks are being reviewed.
asked_by: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
response: Mr Tan Kiat How said the Government does not have access to Mythos and treats AI-enabled cyber risk as an amplification of an existing systemic risk rather than a wholly new category. He said MAS has convened major financial institution CEOs on cyber resilience, and CSA will issue a letter to all CII owners setting expectations including a review of cyber risk posture. He set out five priorities: revisit risk assessments, know your assets, patch faster and monitor continuously, govern AI use, and use AI in defence. Early-warning work includes engaging technology partners, CSA monitoring exploitation patterns, and attack-surface monitoring.

key_points.point: The Government does not have access to Anthropic's Mythos model.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The Government does not have access to Mythos.

key_points.point: Anthropic released Mythos only to a limited set of partners under a controlled preview, and no local bank is known to have access.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Anthropic has released it only to a limited set of partners under a controlled preview, and we are not aware of any local bank that has been granted access.

key_points.point: AI-enabled cyber risk is treated as an amplification of an existing systemic risk, not a wholly new category.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we view AI-enabled cyber risk as an amplification of an existing systemic risk, rather than a wholly new category.

key_points.point: MAS convened the CEOs of major financial institutions to discuss the threat landscape and drive collective action on technology and cyber resilience.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: the Monetary Authority of Singapore has convened the chief executive officers of major financial institutions to discuss the threat landscape and drive collective action on technology and cyber resilience.

key_points.point: CSA will issue a letter to boards and senior leadership of all critical information infrastructure owners today, setting expectations including a review of cyber risk posture.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) will issue a letter to the boards and senior leadership of all critical information infrastructure (CII) owners today.

key_points.point: The first of five priorities is to revisit cybersecurity risk assessments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: First, revisit your cybersecurity risk assessment.

key_points.point: CSA's addendum on Securing Agentic AI, launched in October last year, gives guidance on mapping workflows and applying controls across the life-cycle.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: CSA's addendum on Securing Agentic AI, launched in October last year, sets out practical guidance on mapping workflows and applying controls across the entire life-cycle.

key_points.point: Early-warning work includes engaging technology partners for early visibility and insights into new capabilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: First, we closely engage technology partners for early visibility and insights into new capabilities as they emerge.

key_points.point: Support for SMEs includes CISO-as-a-Service and Cyber Essentials and Cyber Trust Marks.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: This includes the CISO-as-a-Service and the Cyber Essentials and Cyber Trust Marks, which support organisations to assess and improve their security posture.

key_points.point: CSA and other agencies have schemes and programmes to support Singaporeans pursuing cybersecurity careers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: CSA, together with various Government agencies, including our security agencies, have been putting in place different schemes and programmes to support Singaporeans who wish to have a career in cybersecurity.

supplementary: International cooperation, framework adequacy, SME support, talent, and access to frontier AI models.
